WITH bucket_stats AS MATERIALIZED (
    SELECT
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ss_quantity BETWEEN 1 AND 20) AS cnt1,
        AVG(ss_ext_tax) FILTER (WHERE ss_quantity BETWEEN 1 AND 20) AS avg_ext1,
        AVG(ss_net_paid_inc_tax) FILTER (WHERE ss_quantity BETWEEN 1 AND 20) AS avg_net1,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ss_quantity BETWEEN 21 AND 40) AS cnt2,
        AVG(ss_ext_tax) FILTER (WHERE ss_quantity BETWEEN 21 AND 40) AS avg_ext2,
        AVG(ss_net_paid_inc_tax) FILTER (WHERE ss_quantity BETWEEN 21 AND 40) AS avg_net2,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ss_quantity BETWEEN 41 AND 60) AS cnt3,
        AVG(ss_ext_tax) FILTER (WHERE ss_quantity BETWEEN 41 AND 60) AS avg_ext3,
        AVG(ss_net_paid_inc_tax) FILTER (WHERE ss_quantity BETWEEN 41 AND 60) AS avg_net3,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ss_quantity BETWEEN 61 AND 80) AS cnt4,
        AVG(ss_ext_tax) FILTER (WHERE ss_quantity BETWEEN 61 AND 80) AS avg_ext4,
        AVG(ss_net_paid_inc_tax) FILTER (WHERE ss_quantity BETWEEN 61 AND 80) AS avg_net4,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ss_quantity BETWEEN 81 AND 100) AS cnt5,
        AVG(ss_ext_tax) FILTER (WHERE ss_quantity BETWEEN 81 AND 100) AS avg_ext5,
        AVG(ss_net_paid_inc_tax) FILTER (WHERE ss_quantity BETWEEN 81 AND 100) AS avg_net5
    FROM store_sales
)
SELECT
    CASE WHEN cnt1 > 1071 THEN avg_ext1 ELSE avg_net1 END AS bucket1,
    CASE WHEN cnt2 > 39161 THEN avg_ext2 ELSE avg_net2 END AS bucket2,
    CASE WHEN cnt3 > 29434 THEN avg_ext3 ELSE avg_net3 END AS bucket3,
    CASE WHEN cnt4 > 6568 THEN avg_ext4 ELSE avg_net4 END AS bucket4,
    CASE WHEN cnt5 > 21216 THEN avg_ext5 ELSE avg_net5 END AS bucket5
FROM reason
JOIN bucket_stats ON true
WHERE r_reason_sk = 1

reasoning_trace:
1. SINGLE-PASS CONDITIONAL AGGREGATION — TARGET: the repeated `store_sales` scalar subqueries (5 counts + 10 averages across the five `ss_quantity` buckets) — TRANSFORMATION: replace all of them with one aggregate over `store_sales` that computes, for each bucket, `count(*)`, `avg(ss_ext_tax)`, and `avg(ss_net_paid_inc_tax)` using per-range conditional aggregation, then feed those precomputed values into the outer CASEs.

2. SINGLE-EVALUATION ROW SOURCE — TARGET: the outer `FROM reason WHERE r_reason_sk = 1` with five CASE expressions referencing scalar subplans — TRANSFORMATION: put the single-pass aggregate into a derived table/CTE in the FROM clause and cross join it with `reason`, so the expensive aggregate is evaluated exactly once and the single-row output behavior is preserved.

3. COVERING INDEX — TARGET: `store_sales` columns `ss_quantity`, `ss_ext_tax`, `ss_net_paid_inc_tax` — TRANSFORMATION: add a covering b-tree index on `ss_quantity` including the two average columns, so the single aggregate can be served as an index-only scan and avoid heap reads from the wide `store_sales` table.
